decisions.reason: As a 2023 launch still listed in 2024 and strongly related to the firm's established laser-marking know-how, it is likely retained as a complementary workstation product that the firm can improve with its in-house R&D and service capabilities.

The thermal inkjet printer is close to the core coding business, remained on its own page across both years, and fits the firm's strategy of offering application-specific technologies across surfaces and lines.

The piezo inkjet printer also sits near the firm's existing knowledge base and continued standalone presentation suggests enough market relevance to justify further learning and commercial refinement rather than withdrawal.

This 2024 industrial laser marking line is a flagship direction shown on the home page, so given the firm's strong absorptive capacity, growth, and strategic push toward digital traceability it is very unlikely to be removed soon.
The compact laser marking cabin was newly launched in 2024 on its own page and builds directly on the firm's laser portfolio, making continued market development more probable than an early exit.

Although more niche than the others, the lubricant printing system builds on the firm's printing competencies and its trade-fair award gives positive external validation, so the firm would likely keep it while testing and refining the segment.
